::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
Guangdong province's first and only scaled 12-inch wafer fab — the province that consumes an estimated ~40% of China's chips had no domestic 12-inch mass production before CanSemi. Phases 1–3 are in production at ~63,300 wafers/month realized versus 80,000 planned (end-2025), with a third fab (Phase 3, ¥16.25 billion) online since December 2024 and a ¥25.2 billion Phase 4 (third site, 480,000 wafers/year mixed-signal) started January 2026.
:::

**Chinese name:** 粤芯半导体技术股份有限公司 (Yuèxīn Bàndǎotǐ)

## What does this facility make?

Analog/power-management, fingerprint-sensor, display-driver, CIS and power chips on 12-inch wafers — plus, uniquely among mainland foundries, mass-production 12-inch silicon-photonics wafers (90nm platform feeding 400G/800G/1.6T optical modules).

## Why does it matter?

Its IPO cleared the ChiNext listing committee in June 2026 as the board's first pre-profit wafer-fab listing under Standard 3, with CSRC registration approved 28 August 2026 — a template for funding loss-making specialty fabs with public markets. Prospectus coverage shows revenues of ¥1.044/1.681/2.582 billion (2023-2025) against net losses of ¥1.917/2.253/2.346 billion, with earliest guided profitability in 2029 — how capital-hungry the model is.

## Project Timeline

- **Sep 2019** — Phase 1 enters production, ~18 months after groundbreaking
- **Dec 2024** — Phase 3 (second fab, ¥16.25 billion, +40,000 wafers/month) line activated
- **Jan 2026** — Phase 4 (¥25.2 billion, 480,000 wafers/year mixed-signal, nodes roadmap to 65-22nm) formally started
- **Jun 2026** — ChiNext IPO approved by listing committee — first pre-profit wafer fab on the board
- **Aug 2026** — CSRC registration approval received for the IPO (planned raise ¥7.5 billion)
